title: Why each invalid example must be rejected
description: scripts/verify.mjs asserts two things per case: that the mapped schema rejects the document, and that the rejection names the keyword below. Without the second assertion a fixture could 'pass' by tripping an unrelated rule and the intended trap would stay untested.

server.vision-over-ws.mustReject: xtls-rprx-vision is only defined over raw TCP. Compiling it anyway yields a config Xray accepts and ignores, i.e. a server the user believes is XTLS-protected that is not (docs/architecture/23).

server.reality-with-privatekey.mustReject: A client configuration must never contain the REALITY private key. It belongs to the server operator; sync it to a laptop and every machine with the profile can mint handshakes (docs/architecture/32).

server.inline-headers.mustReject: Header maps may carry Authorization or Cookie, so they are keystore references only. This is SEC-1 (omega-target/src/options.coffee:27 strips 'headers' from nothing) closed at the schema boundary.

server.security-none-with-tls.mustReject: A tls block under security none is either a mistake or a smuggled SNI; either way the compiler would emit settings Xray never reads.

server.h2-without-tls.mustReject: h2 requires TLS by definition; an h2-over-cleartext config is not a thing Xray will run.

server.missing-user-id-ref.mustReject: A VLESS server without a user id cannot authenticate. Required rather than nullable so no code path can present a half-built server as ready.

profile.no-servers.mustReject: An empty ConnectorProfile compiles to an inbound with no outbound behind it -- a guaranteed dead profile that still occupies the switcher.

profile.fixed-without-default.mustReject: mode fixed means exactly one server; without defaultServerId there is nothing to pin.

profile.failopen-without-confirm.mustReject: failOpen is the one setting that lets traffic escape when the Core dies, so it requires the user's confirmation token (ADR-0009).

subscription.http-url.mustReject: A plaintext subscription feed can be rewritten in flight into a config that points every profile at an attacker's server.

subscription.url-userinfo.mustReject: Credentials in the URL are stored, synced and echoed into logs verbatim. They belong in headersRef, which is a keystore pointer.

subscription.url-token.mustReject: ?token= is a credential wearing the shape of an address. This namespace is sync-eligible and url is required, so a raw token URL reaches the browser account, the Gist and WebDAV in clear -- the SEC-1 leak again, one field over. The address goes in urlRef and url keeps a sanitised display form (docs/architecture/29 §4).

subscription.keep-last-good-false.mustReject: Discarding the working list on a failed refresh is the bug the master prompt forbids; the flag is not a user preference.

subscription.oversized-limit.mustReject: The guard has to be smaller than the damage. 16 MB accepted here means a feed can DoS the parser with no ceiling (SEC-2).

routing.unknown-condition.mustReject: Only the twelve registry types in omega-pac/src/conditions.coffee round-trip through the legacy engine; an invented one silently matches nothing.

routing.invented-outbound.mustReject: A rule may name only 'direct', 'block' or a derived srv-<uuid8> tag. Free-text outbounds let a policy point at a tag the compiler never emitted.

routing.prefixed-profilename.mustReject: SwitchProfile stores bare names; Profiles.nameAsKey adds the '+'. Writing '+direct' here produces a rule that can never match.

events.unknown-name.mustReject: The event set is closed so UI code cannot bind to an event that exists on one build only (docs/architecture/36).

pins.mirror-url.mustReject: Only the pinned upstream release host is legal. A mirror is a supply-chain decision and would defeat the whole pin (ADR-0019).

envelope.ok-without-result.mustReject: ok true without a result is an answer that says nothing happened; the client cannot tell it from a dropped reply (docs/architecture/25).

envelope.event-with-method.mustReject: method is a request field. An event carrying one would be dispatched as a command by a naive receiver (ADR-0007).

failure-policy.global-failopen.mustReject: ADR-0009 rule 2: fail-open is a per-profile exception only. A global coreDeath.action of failOpen is a product whose default is unproxied traffic whenever Core dies, and no confirmToken in this document could make that an informed choice for profiles the user never looked at (docs/architecture/30-failure-policy.md).

failure-policy.teardown-restore.mustReject: serviceTeardown is a Connector-triggered plane, so its terminal resolution cannot be 'restore': restoring the browser's pre-NEXORA setting is the direct/system egress that forbiddenOutcomes forbids. 'restore' is legal under extensionLifecycle, where the user is the trigger.

failure-policy.narrow-forbidden.mustReject: forbiddenOutcomes may be omitted, in which case the default is the full set, but it may not be narrowed: a policy that names two of the three leaks is a policy with an escape hatch written in JSON.
